🧠 Crypto News Brief: Rising Treasury yields, pricier oil and fresh Fed-hike bets pulled Bitcoin back to $83K. Yet the institutional pipeline keeps widening, from Coinbase's new clearinghouse and Citi's stablecoin rails to Blockchain.com's IPO push. 📉 Bitcoin Slips to $83K as Yields and Oil Stoke Fed-Hike Fears Bitcoin fell to just above $83,000 early Tuesday as climbing U.S. Treasury yields and a second straight day of rising oil prices revived inflation worries and bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike. The pressure followed President Trump's rejection of Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and traders are now bracing for Wednesday's PCE inflation print. Zcash led losses among major tokens with a 12% drop, while crypto sentiment gauges remain in "greed" territory, in sharp contrast with the fear gripping equities. Read full story 🏛️ CFTC Clears Coinbase to Run Its Own USDC-Native Clearinghouse The CFTC registered Coinbase Clearing LLC as a derivatives clearing organization on September 28, completing Coinbase's in-house U.S. derivatives stack of exchange, broker and clearinghouse. The approval covers only fully collateralized futures, options on futures and swaps, using USDC as collateral with 24/7 settlement. Margined products and the upcoming single-stock perpetuals will continue to rely on outside clearing partners. More details 🏦 Citi Opens Its Checkout to Stablecoins via Coinbase Citi's institutional clients can now accept stablecoin payments through the bank's Spring by Citi merchant platform, with Coinbase running the blockchain rails and converting tokens into fiat before Citi settles the funds. In the other direction, Coinbase Virtual Accounts will run on Citi's Virtual Account Wallet, automatically converting incoming fiat into stablecoins. Both products launch first in the U.S., expanding a partnership the two firms started in October 2025. Read more 📈 Blockchain.com Targets $500M IPO at Up to $6B Valuation Blockchain.com is pitching investors on a U.S. listing before year-end, aiming to raise about $500 million at a valuation of $4 billion to $6 billion, according to Bloomberg. That is well below the $14 billion the company commanded in 2022. Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** Anthropic dropped its second model in a week, and it's almost as good as the one it launched last Tuesday for half the price. OpenAI scrapped its next model because it wasn't honest about what it did. Florida wants a judge to stop OpenAI from building new models at all. And Anthropic's IPO filing leaked, with a loss number that looks a lot scarier than it is.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Anthropic:** How close is Sonnet 5.5 to Opus?

* **OpenAI:** What did GPT-6.1 Astra do that got it cancelled?

* **Florida:** Can a state stop OpenAI from building AI?

* **Anthropic:** How do you lose $42 billion and ask for $2 trillion?


----------







----------
## Claude Sonnet 5.5 is almost Opus for half the price

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7dfce945-01dc-4ab9-9c5a-b6de049cb104/Sep_29_-_1.jpg?t=1790671124)
Caption: 

Anthropic [released Sonnet 5.5](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5), its second new model in less than a week. It's the mid-size Claude, and it's now nearly as good as Opus 5.5, the big one.
